title: Peasants' Revolt Adventure
welcome_lead: In 1381 furious peasants marched on London. Meet Wat Tyler, John Ball, and young King Richard II in the Peasants' Revolt. 🔥
meta_desc: Peasants' Revolt Adventure — a KS3 History walkthrough of the 1381 rising. Poll tax, Wat Tyler and Richard II.
final_note: You learned the causes of the 1381 revolt, the role of Wat Tyler and John Ball, and how Richard II tricked the rebels.

walkthroughs.body_html:
After the Black Death of 1348–49, far fewer workers were left, so peasants wanted higher wages.

The government tried to freeze wages and tie peasants to the land. Then it added a hated new poll tax in 1381 — every adult had to pay the same, whether rich or poor.

For poor families this was crushing. Anger boiled over in Essex and Kent. 😡

In June 1381, rebels led by Wat Tyler marched on London. The priest John Ball preached that 'When Adam delved and Eve span, who was then the gentleman?' — meaning everyone should be equal.

The rebels burned the Savoy Palace, opened prisons and killed the Archbishop of Canterbury and the king's treasurer.

King Richard II was only 14 years old. 👑

Richard II bravely met the rebels at Smithfield. He promised to end serfdom and lower taxes.

During the meeting, Wat Tyler was killed by the Mayor of London. The peasants went home — but Richard broke every promise.

Rebel leaders were hunted down and hanged. Yet the revolt scared the rulers, and within a hundred years serfdom faded away in England.
